title: Early-Stage Cervical Cancer & Radical Hysterectomy
subject: ss-gynaecological-oncology
refs: DeVita, Hellman, and Rosenberg's Cancer: Principles & Practice of Oncology 11e Ch 83
NCCN Clinical Practice Guidelines in Oncology: Cervical Cancer (2024)

steps.say: Surgical resection of early invasive cervical neoplasms follows standardized anatomical classification frameworks. Modern practice utilizes the Querleu Morrow schema to define the lateral and caudal margins of parametrial excision.
steps.tx: The anatomical **Querleu-Morrow classification** standardizes radical hysterectomy into four tiers. **Type A resection** entails minimal pericervical resection, **Type B ureteral unroofing** transects paracervical tissue at the unroofed ureter, and **Type C complete resection** requires complete excision of the ventral and dorsal parametria directly to the internal iliac vessels and pelvic sidewall.

steps.say: The choice of surgical access route underwent a profound paradigm shift following high level prospective evidence. Laparotomy demonstrated clear survival superiority over laparoscopic and robotic approaches.
steps.tx: The prospective phase **3** **LACC trial** published by **Ramirez 2018** established **open radical hysterectomy superiority** (three-year disease-free survival **97.1** percent) over minimally invasive laparoscopy or robotics, which exhibited **inferior survival minimally invasive** (disease-free survival **91.2** percent) and a fourfold increase in locoregional pelvic recurrences.

left.title: Open Abdominal Approach (LACC Gold Standard)
points: Avoids tumor rupture from uterine manipulators
Absence of CO2 pneumoperitoneum tumor dissemination

right.title: Minimally Invasive Surgery (Laparoscopic / Robotic)
points: Fourfold escalation in locoregional pelvic recurrences
Restricted or contraindicated for standard curative resections

steps.say: Postoperative histological examination determines whether patients require supplementary pelvic radiotherapy. Specific intermediate risk factors combine tumor dimension with deep myometrial and vascular penetration.
steps.tx: Following radical hysterectomy, **Sedlis criteria** from protocol **GOG 92** identify intermediate-risk pathological features mandating **adjuvant pelvic radiation**. Validated criteria evaluate combinations of **outer third stromal invasion** (deep third), positive **LVSI**, and clinical tumor diameter >=**4** cm, which reduce recurrence risk from 28 percent to 15 percent when treated.

steps.say: Adverse pathological findings at the surgical margins or nodal stations indicate biologically aggressive disease. In these situations combined chemoradiotherapy delivers superior local control compared to radiation alone.
steps.tx: The landmark **Peters criteria** established by protocol **GOG 109** mandate postoperative **concurrent cisplatin chemoradiotherapy** (weekly cisplatin 40 mg/m2) for high-risk pathology: pathologically **positive nodes** (pelvic lymph node metastasis), microscopic parametrial involvement, or **positive margins** on the vaginal cuff, conferring a marked survival advantage.

nodes.label: Identify positive lymph nodes, parametrial spread, or close margins
Initiate external beam pelvic radiation (45 to 50.4 Gy)
Deliver concurrent weekly intravenous cisplatin (40 mg/m2)

steps.say: Preservation of autonomous pelvic neuroanatomy minimizes long term voiding and anorectal morbidity. Careful dissection isolates the hypogastric nerves and splanchnic fibers within the paracervical connective tissues.
steps.tx: In **nerve-sparing radical hysterectomy** (**Type C1**), meticulous surgical dissection preserves the **inferior hypogastric plexus** and bilateral **pelvic splanchnic nerves S2-S4** along with the sympathetic hypogastric trunks, preserving parasympathetic detrusor innervation and preventing severe post-operative urinary retention in tier **1**, **2**, or **4** pelvic operations.

nodes.label: Identify hypogastric nerve trunk lateral to rectovaginal septum
Preserve pelvic splanchnic roots from sacral roots S2-S4
Separate bladder branches from lateral cardinal ligament
Achieve radical resection margins while sparing vesical motor nerves

steps.say: Microinvasive lesions without vascular invasion harbor an exceedingly low probability of regional lymphatic metastasis. Conservative surgical excision or simple extrafascial hysterectomy achieves curative oncological outcomes.
steps.tx: For microscopic **Stage IA1** squamous disease without lymphovascular space invasion (stromal invasion depth <=3 mm), regional nodal metastasis occurs in under **1** percent. Curative management consists of therapeutic **conization** with negative surgical margins or extrafascial **simple hysterectomy**, delivering an exceptional **cure rate >99%** (**99** percent).

left.title: Stage IA1 without LVSI (Depth <=3 mm)
points: Diagnostic and therapeutic cervical conization curative
Extrafascial simple hysterectomy if childbearing complete

right.title: Stage IA1 with LVSI or Stage IA2 (3 to 5 mm)
points: Risk of nodal metastasis rises to 3 to 5%
Requires modified radical hysterectomy (Querleu-Morrow Type B)
Mandatory pelvic lymph node assessment or sentinel node biopsy

steps.say: Deeper microinvasion or lymphovascular penetration requires wider parametrial tissue margins. Modified radical surgery clears the paracervical tissues up to the unroofed ureter combined with regional nodal sampling.
steps.tx: When **Stage IA1** exhibits lymphovascular space invasion or progresses to **Stage IA2** (depth >3 mm to <=5 mm), risk of pelvic nodal involvement increases to 3 to 5 percent. Standard intervention shifts to **modified radical hysterectomy** (**Type B** resection) with systematic **pelvic lymphadenectomy** clearing tissue medial to the unroofed ureters.

steps.say: Premenopausal women with non squamous cervical histologies can undergo surgical preservation of gonadal function. The ovaries are repositioned into the upper paracolic gutters beyond prospective pelvic radiation fields.
steps.tx: In **premenopausal squamous** cell carcinoma requiring adjuvant pelvic radiotherapy, surgical **ovarian transposition** (**oophoropexy**) transposes the ovaries to achieve **pelvic brim clearance** at least **2** to **3** cm above the pelvic brim and **4** cm from prospective radiation fields, preserving functional endocrine activity in over eighty percent of patients.
